title: Ops Safety Orchestration Studio: cross-functional playbook and sprint plan
content:
Purpose
-----
This doc is a working playbook for a cross-functional initiative we’re calling the Ops Safety Orchestration Studio (OSOS). Goal: create a small, repeatable program that helps feature teams adopt SLOs, onboard minimal alerting and runbooks, and complete a first safety rollout within 6–8 weeks. This is intentionally lightweight: the studio provides templates, paired engineering time, and a curated runbook/telemetry checklist to unblock teams that ship model-serving or inference-facing features.

High-level outcomes (success metrics)
- 8 feature services with meaningful SLOs + runbooks within 8 weeks of engagement start
- Reduction in alert noise for participating teams by 30% within first 30 days after rollout
- Standardized SLI collector (trace/span + token success/latency) deployed to prod for each service
- Playbook validated with at least two Dedicated/private deployment customers for compliance feedback

Scope of the studio
- Onboarding: pairing sessions (SRE + feature team) to select SLIs and set SLO targets
- Instrumentation: telemetry checklist, minimal dashboards, and error-budget export to console/alerting
- Runbooks: templated runbook + incident escalation matrix
- Rollout: canary SLO enforcement (alerting thresholds + temporary overrides) and stakeholder comms
- Close-loop: post-rollout retrospective and quality regression check tied to Redwood Optimize signals

Who should join (roles)
- Feature team service owner (engineer) — required
- Product/PM — optional but recommended for customer-impact decisions
- SRE buddy — required (pairing, runbook authoring)
- Observability engineer — required for dashboard and SLI plumbing
- Solutions eng/Support — invited for customer-facing features or Dedicated customers

Studio flow (6–8 week template)
1) Intake (week 0): 30–45m kickoff + readiness checklist. Deliverables: service contact, current SLIs (if any), current pager volume, top 3 customer journeys.
2) Discovery & SLI design (week 1): choose 2–3 candidate SLIs (latency p95/p99, request success rate, model response validity signal). Draft SLO targets and error budget policy. Deliverable: SLO spec doc + Jira ticket created (example: SRE-OSOS-<service>-slo-spec).
3) Instrumentation sprint (weeks 2–3): implement SLI collectors, add tags, add trace hooks. If missing, add token-level counters in gateway/service. Deliverable: instrumentation PR + dashboard stub.
4) Runbook & Alerts (week 3–4): author one-page runbook, map oncall, configure alerting thresholds that reflect error budget burn rates. Deliverable: runbook + alert rule PR.
5) Canary rollout (week 4–6): enable SLO alerts in canary mode for 48–72h, monitor regression signals (quality and latency), decide go/no-go. Deliverable: rollout decision log + stakeholder email template.
6) Post-rollout retro (week 6–8): summarize learnings, adjust thresholds, codify follow-ups into backlog. Deliverable: retro notes + team adoption checklist completed.

Suggested SLO templates (starter values, change per service)
- Latency SLO (user-facing inference): 95th percentile < 300ms 99% of the time (SLO: p95 < 300ms over 30d window -> target 99.0%)
- Success SLO (API-level): request success rate >= 99.95% over 30d window (target 99.95%)
- Quality SLO (model-level heuristic): proportion of responses passing safety/format check >= 99.0% over 7d sliding window
Notes: these are opinionated starting points. During discovery we map customer impact and may choose longer windows or hybrid objectives (rolling 7d for quality regressions, 30d for latency).

Instrumentation checklist (minimal)
- Request id propagated through all services
- Token-level or request-level success/failure counter (ok/error/timeout)
- Latency histograms with p50/p95/p99 buckets
- Synthetic probes for critical flows (daily smoke job)
- Error budget burn metric exported to console and available via API
- Trace sampling for p99 tails enabled

Runbook checklist (one page)
- Service summary (owner, critical customer journeys)
- Primary SLOs and current burn rate
- How to reproduce most common errors locally
- First response steps for noise vs real degradation
- Escalation contacts and paging rules
- Post-incident follow-ups (RCA owner, timeline)

Alerting guidance
- Prefer attentional alerts: low-frequency, high-actionability
- Example pairing:
  - Immediate page: request success < 99.8% over 5m AND errors > 50 req/min
  - Pager if error budget burn rate > 15% per hour AND sustained for 30m
  - Page for infra saturation (GPU OOM/queue backlog) even if SLO holds
- Add a ‘noisy-alert’ suppression sprint if a service is known to be noisy; use temporary annotation and re-evaluate in retro

Communications & stakeholder cadence
- Weekly standup with feature + SRE during instrumentation phase
- Biweekly review with product/solutions for prioritization
- Standardized rollout email templates (canary start, canary stop, full roll) stored in confluence link above
- Slack channel: #ops-safety-studio-<service> created on intake

Risk & mitigation notes
- Risk: teams treat SLO as gate and freeze product changes. Mitigation: emphasize SLO as learning tool; default to “monitor first, enforce later”.
- Risk: telemetry gaps expose false positives. Mitigation: require synthetic probes + manual verification step before paging.
- Risk: model-quality regressions are subtle and not captured by simple heuristics. Mitigation: add small human-in-the-loop sampling for first 2 weeks post-rollout and enlarge signal set for Redwood Optimize.

Dependencies and non-goals
- We do NOT ship a full rules engine; we recommend teams use existing alerting backends (PagerDuty, Opsgenie) and Console’s error-budget dashboard.
- Dependency on observability infra to add error-budget export endpoints (ticket: JIRA-10012)

Playbook artifacts to produce (templates and examples)
- SLO spec template (YAML) — minimal fields: name, SLI query, window, target, owner
- Runbook template (markdown)
- Alerting rule examples (promql/snql) for latency and success
- Synthetic probe recipe and CI job example
- Oncall pairing checklist and recording template for handoffs

Quick wins (first 2 weeks)
- Pair on a single synthetic probe and dashboard (takes <4 hours)
- Agree on 1 latency SLO and create the Jira SLO spec ticket
- Deploy error-budget export to Console for one service and validate pull-through in Slack report

Open questions / decisions to make
- Should we default to a 30d or 7d window for new services? (ops: 30d; rapid-feedback teams prefer 7d) — decision owner: Priya Nair
- What is the minimum telemetry budget we can require without blocking releases? (proposal: request-level counters + p95 histogram)
- Do we want an opt-in list of Dedicated customers for regulatory validation? (proposal: yes; solutions eng to track)

Immediate next steps (action list)
- Aisha: finalize this doc and link SLO YAML template to Confluence (due: 2027-05-05)
- Miguel: create JIRA epic OSOS-1 and add intake form (due: 2027-05-07)
- Priya: schedule intake slots for May/June and coordinate product stakeholder invites (due: 2027-05-08)
- Observability eng (Ethan): stub error-budget export endpoint + example dashboard (due: 2027-05-14)
- Sofie: draft rollout email templates and slack channel naming conventions (due: 2027-05-06)

Notes to self / meeting fragments
- 2027-05-03 kickoff: ask infra about trace sampling cost; suggest 0.5% default for p99 tails
- Customer ask: Dedicated customers want explicit audit log of SLO changes — add to compliance checklist
- Consider a small pilot with the embeddings pipeline team — high customer exposure and measurable latency profile

Appendix: example SLO spec (text)
name: inference-latency-p95
owner: service-team@example.com
sl i_query: "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))"
window: 30d
target: 0.99
error_budget_policy: "alert when burn_rate > 10% per hour for 60m"

-- end of working doc --
